findings.failure_path: Human approval of AI-generated runtime configuration is classified as outside design scope. For a design-only request for a service that generates and activates tenant permission or quota policies, that approval is an architectural state transition. The mapped runtime controls do not establish it. This is a third uncovered obligation, contradicting the subsequent claim that only two obligations lack coverage.
findings.smallest_fix: Preserve existing runtime-configuration approval requirements in the architecture contract and correct the coverage table; distinguish these from invented approval of the design document.

findings.failure_path: The declared unchanged gate prohibits two fewer successes, but both Node.js checks decline from five successes to three. Unequal sample counts explain why this is not evidence of behavioral regression; they do not satisfy the original gate. The disclosed post-hoc comparison evaluates a different acceptance rule.
findings.smallest_fix: Explicitly mark the original gate unmet or inconclusive, and separate any decision to adopt a rate-based comparison from the original acceptance result.

findings.failure_path: The replacement accounting measures whole-file sizes for touched files, not bytes actually loaded. Reading 1 KB from a 100 KB baseline file versus an entire 30 KB candidate file would report a reduction while actual input grows. The reported medians therefore do not establish passage of the loaded-byte gate without its missing measurement definition and read evidence.
findings.smallest_fix: Provide comparable accounting of delivered content, or explicitly define and accept the whole-file proxy as a revised metric rather than declaring the original gate passed.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the reported design-document evaluations and generic validation summaries do not demonstrate mixed-request routing, re-entry before implementation, requester-only security facts, or preservation of existing approvals. A security heading and fewer role mentions can score successfully while those requirements fail; no bounded scenarios or assertions establish otherwise.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply candidate-bound adversarial cases and observable results covering these transitions, including an unavailable trust-root fact and an already-required approval.

challenge_focus: Adversarially test new routing and design rules: a design-only backend request now starts at software-architecture without loading product-rd-workflow, including on money, permission and data-isolation surfaces, and product-rd takes over before implementation; security questions are answered by the designer; open points get stated defaults; handoffs name a stage, never a person, and no approver or sign-off is invented. Find a request these rules misroute (design plus implementation in one ask, a multi-stage delivery, a non-backend design), a case where forbidding questions makes the designer guess something only the requester knows, a case where the no-sign-off rule suppresses an approval the repository or request did require, and any claim in plan sections 11.5-11.6 the recorded numbers do not support.
